transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: Mon Sep 29 2025
- Time: 15:00 PT (approx)
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Ana Torres (Redwood CSM); Daniel Reyes (Hightree), Priya Kapoor (Hightree), Jordan Miles (Hightree), Sofia Alvarez (Hightree Finance), Samir Nair (Hightree Security)

Optional summary (auto):
- Focus: review current usage and spike patterns, prioritize dedicated capacity vs hosted options, align on pilot scope and next steps for cost optimization and reliability proofs.
- Main outcomes: Redwood to send three cost/sizing options; SE to prepare pilot plan; customer to share traffic samples and security constraints.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Patel: Okay thanks everyone for joining, we're gonna kick off. hi hi this is Maya from Redwood, thanks for doing the capacity workshop.
[00:00:08] Daniel Reyes: Hey Maya, thanks, we've got the key folks on the line. Daniel here, head of ML.
[00:00:12] Priya Kapoor: Priya - platform engineering, we wanted to make sure we walk through the spikes last quarter and the cost implications.
[00:00:18] Maya Patel: Great, quick agenda - usage patterns and recent anomalies, cost tradeoffs and reserved vs burst, reliability concerns and SLA, security constraints (VPC/KMS), pilot plan and runbook, next steps. Sound ok?
[00:00:30] Jordan Miles: Yes that's perfect.
[00:00:33] Liam Chen: Quick intro from me - Liam, SE. I'll propose some pilot perf cases and suggest batching/kv cache config tweaks.
[00:00:40] Sofia Alvarez: I'm mostly here to understand the numbers and the options so we can budget.

[00:01:05] Priya Kapoor: To kick off — we saw two big spikes in July and Aug, about 3x our baseline qps for an hour each, plus a 20 minute tail. We hit throttling on the hosted tier once, which was... uh, a surprise.
[00:01:22] Maya Patel: Right, we pulled logs — there were a couple of concurrent large-context long-chain requests that drove token cost. We flagged fallback to a lighter variant but it didn't kick quickly enough. That's something we can address with routing policies.
[00:01:40] Daniel Reyes: We're also seeing variability in seq lengths — some customer flows hit 1.2k tokens and others are short. That makes batching harder.
[00:01:49] Liam Chen: Yep and that will affect kernel selection, latency SLOs. For the pilot I want to capture a realistic distribution, so thanks Priya for offering the samples.

[00:02:15] Sofia Alvarez: Quick question on pricing — what are the levers? We heard about reserved capacity and then on-demand bursting which costs more. Can you show bluntly the delta?
[00:02:25] Maya Patel: Absolutely — reserved (Dedicated) gives predictable unit cost per token and committed monthly spend; burst is metered at hosted rates which are higher. We'll send a three-option sheet: (1) Fully hosted with burst caps, (2) Dedicated baseline + limited burst, (3) Dedicated + extended burst and standby nodes. Each will include projected monthly cost for your current traffic and two spike scenarios.

[00:03:05] Jordan Miles: For option 2, how quickly can we ramp from baseline to burst? We need <30s for critical flows.
[00:03:12] Liam Chen: With our Dedicated pools we can do autoscale with pre-warm strategies; if you reserve a small standby pool we can shift within 20-40s depending on model load and KVcache warm-up. Note: cold KV cache will incur a token/time penalty.
[00:03:30] Daniel Reyes: KV cache? I heard KV cache as K V in some docs as "KVcach" and it confused an engineer.
[00:03:36] Maya Patel: Yeah sorry the auto transcript mislabels — KV cache (key-value cache). We'll clarify the doc.

[00:04:10] Priya Kapoor: On security the SSO is already via Okta but we need SAML assertion examples and KMS integration; Samir is checking HSM requirements.
[00:04:20] Samir Nair: For us, data-at-rest must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK) and audit logs retained for 365 days. Also we need to validate whether private deploy (on-prem or VPC) is necessary for payment flows.
[00:04:35] Maya Patel: We support KMS integrations and VPC Private deployment. For the SOC2 and audit logs we can share the redacted artifact pack — will include retention options.

[00:05:05] Liam Chen: Back to reliability — you mentioned throttling in hosted. We should look at routing policies: route critical endpoints to Dedicated with failover to a lighter hosted model. That keeps latency tight but reduces cost for non-critical flows.
[00:05:18] Daniel Reyes: What's the expected P95 improvement if we move critical flows to dedicated?
[00:05:24] Liam Chen: In our benchmarks for similarly sized profiles we saw P95 drop from ~450ms to ~150-220ms for generation under 512 tokens when on Dedicated with pre-warmed caches and batching tuned. For longer sequences it's less dramatic but still material.
[00:05:41] Sofia Alvarez: That's helpful. Can you quantify savings from KV caching and batching?
[00:05:47] Liam Chen: Roughly you can see 15-40% token cost reduction depending on request locality. If you have many repeated prefixes, prefix caching helps a lot. We'll simulate in pilot.

[00:06:20] Jordan Miles: Pilot scope — we're thinking a 72-hour controlled run with representative traffic, two failure modes (network blip, one node reboot), and a stress window to simulate spike. Can Redwood run that in a sandbox?
[00:06:32] Maya Patel: Yes, we can run a pilot in a dedicated sandbox environment. We'll provide a runbook and metrics dashboard; SE will operate tests with you. That will also show autoscale times.

[00:07:05] Daniel Reyes: For the pilot we need to measure: latency distributions (P50/P95/P99), token consumption per request, cold vs warm cache penalties, and ramp times.
[00:07:14] Liam Chen: We'll make sure those are in the test matrix. Also will include one test at 1.5x baseline sustained for 30m and a rapid 3x 5-minute spike.

[00:07:42] Priya Kapoor: Onboarding timeline — security sign-off is typically 2 weeks, procurement a week after. We're targeting go/no-go on reserved commitment in mid-October.
[00:07:52] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get the cost options and security docs to you by Friday.

[00:08:25] Sofia Alvarez: A nit on billing — do you offer monthly smoothing or annual prepay discounts?
[00:08:32] Maya Patel: Yes annual commitments get better unit pricing; also we can structure a phased ramp with an initial three-month pilot discount. We'll lay that out.

[00:09:05] Samir Nair: A security question — in private deployment, can audit logs be pushed to our SIEM and can we use our own KMS cluster?
[00:09:14] Liam Chen: Yes to both; you can either forward logs to your SIEM or opt to store with us with long-term retention. For KMS you can bring your own keys via supported KMS providers; we'll document the flow.

[00:09:42] Jordan Miles: Any risk with model rollouts and regressions? We can't afford quality regressions if you swap model variants in a fallback.
[00:09:50] Maya Patel: We have rollout controls and can tie regressions to prompt sets with automatic rollback. For critical flows, we recommend pinning a model version with canary on 1% before gradual rollout.

[00:10:15] Daniel Reyes: On telemetry — will we get token-level and per-route cost breakdowns?
[00:10:19] Ana Torres: Yes — Redwood Console gives token-level cost by route/model and you can export. We'll include example screenshots.

[00:10:48] Priya Kapoor: For capacity planning, what are realistic minimums for Dedicated? We don't want to overcommit.
[00:10:56] Maya Patel: Minimums depend on model family and throughput. I'll let Liam give ballpark numbers for your profile.
[00:11:02] Liam Chen: For a modest LLM (~15B class) to serve your baseline of ~120 qps of short requests, you'd be looking at X GPUs as baseline (we'll put concrete numbers in the cost sheet). There's a step function as you add concurrency; we can show a few right-sized configs.

[00:11:28] Sofia Alvarez: Can you also show an example invoice line itemization? Finance needs that to sign off.
[00:11:33] Maya Patel: We'll attach a sample invoice breakdown with reserved+burst and credits applied.

[00:12:05] Daniel Reyes: A quick ops question — during the Aug spike when throttling happened did you see any errors or was it graceful degradation?
[00:12:13] Maya Patel: Logs show elevated 429s on one route — that was when request routing overwhelmed the hosted pool. There was also increased latency for other routes. We recommend a routing guardrail to route critical endpoints off-hosted in that case.

[00:12:45] Priya Kapoor: Does Redwood support per-route fallback policies so we can failover to a cheaper model that's still acceptable for non-critical UX?
[00:12:52] Liam Chen: Yes per-route fallback policies are supported and can be configured with A/B testing and canary rules.

[00:13:20] Jordan Miles: For the pilot, can you also include a quality evaluation — we need basic evals so we know fallback doesn't regress.
[00:13:27] Maya Patel: Absolutely — we'll include prompt-set evals and automated regression alerts.

[00:14:05] Samir Nair: When you say "automated regression alerts" is that integrated into our Slack and ticketing?
[00:14:12] Ana Torres: We can push alerts to webhooks, Slack, and create incidents in supported ticketing systems.

[00:14:40] Priya Kapoor: A technical nit: we use Kubernetes and have EKS with private subnets. If we opt for Private deployment, what's the footprint?
[00:14:49] Liam Chen: For VPC private deployment we provide an AMI/helm chart, and the typical on-prem footprint is N GPUs per shard; we'll provide resource docs. For air-gapped we have a packaged bundle but that adds some lead time.

[00:15:20] Sofia Alvarez: Ok finance question again — if we go Dedicated + small burst, what's the expected 12-month spend delta vs staying hosted?
[00:15:30] Maya Patel: It depends on your committed baseline. Often customers see 20-45% unit cost improvement over hosted if they commit to a sustained baseline. But again we'll run your numbers and include sensitivity for spikes.

[00:16:00] Daniel Reyes: Can you share an example of customers who used a hybrid approach? We want a reference.
[00:16:07] Maya Patel: We can anonymize a case study; I mentioned earlier a retail customer that did Dedicated for checkout and hosted for discovery flows — they reduced 35% unit cost and improved P95 for checkout. I'll pull a short anonymized note.

[00:16:40] Priya Kapoor: Ok, timeline and owners — can we recap?
[00:16:45] Maya Patel: Sure. I'll send cost options + invoice sample + SOC2 docs by Friday. Liam will send the pilot runbook and perf matrix by Friday as well. Priya will send traffic profile and seq length samples by Wednesday. Samir to confirm KMS/HSM questions early next week.

[00:17:10] Jordan Miles: And the pilot window you suggested — next week or the week after?
[00:17:15] Maya Patel: We'll be flexible but aiming for next week if security sign-off is green; otherwise week after.

[00:17:30] Sofia Alvarez: One more question — do you offer a cost guardrail that prevents spend overage? We need monthly budget protection.
[00:17:37] Maya Patel: Yes budgets with hard caps and alerts are supported; we can set rate limits and circuit breakers as an extra guardrail.

[00:18:05] Daniel Reyes: Anything else we should be aware of from Redwood roadmap that impacts us?
[00:18:12] Maya Patel: Roadmap highlights: improved autoscale policies, faster cache warm-up strategies, and expanded private deployment templates. None will break existing APIs; we'll share a short roadmap note.

[00:18:40] Priya Kapoor: Great, that helps with our planning.

[00:19:05] Liam Chen: One small technical caveat — quantized model variants may change latency slightly, and quantization profiles will be part of the opt recommendations in the cost sheet.
[00:19:17] Daniel Reyes: We're ok with that as long as we get evals.

[00:19:45] Maya Patel: Final recap on next steps: cost options + invoice + SOC2 by Fri (Maya), pilot runbook + perf cases (Liam) by Fri, traffic samples (Priya) by Wed, security KMS confirmation (Samir) by next Mon. We'll schedule the 72-hour pilot once security gives go.

[00:20:10] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks all.
[00:20:15] Jordan Miles: Thanks.
[00:20:17] Daniel Reyes: Appreciate it.

[00:20:30] --- End of main discussion; rest of call was scheduling and quick clarifications ---

[00:21:05] (side chat - short clarifying Q/A and link shares)
[00:21:10] Maya Patel: I'll drop links to the security pack and the pilot template in the follow-up email.
[00:21:15] Ana Torres: Also post the example dashboard screenshot.

[00:22:00] [closing] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the pilot planning session.
